digest.component_or_area: code-review gate dispatch and LLM model-class wiring
propositions: The code-review gate ignores the per-step model class declared on its five LLM-calling steps, running every pass on the single resolved cfg.model.
The usage log records only the prompt name (op) and cannot attribute a call to a step, since base and the round_a/round_b batch finder share the code-review-base prompt.
Step 0 adds observability: a ContextVar carrying the step id and raw declared class token so usage_log.record() writes step and model_class additively, inert when REBAR_USAGE_LOG is unset.
The plan-review gate honours classes because it wraps run_workflow in gate_config(cfg), while the code-review dispatch path omits that scope.

An offline end-to-end recording-runner test, injected beneath the production RunnerAgentStep, must assert each step receives its declared class under a class table differing from cfg.model and be confirmed RED before the fix.
The defect is pre-existing and not a regression: verify has declared model: standard since story 172e yet ran on opus; declarations in code-review.yaml must not change.
